issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold ticking
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping sound from the engine bay, loudest on a cold start and fading as the engine warms up. Over time you may smell exhaust or hear it get louder, and some vans need the repair more than once.
issues.why: The cast-iron exhaust manifolds on Nissan's 5.6L V8 expand and shrink with every heat cycle and eventually crack, or the studs holding them snap. Heavy work use and long idling make it worse.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm where the leak is before it grows. A small crack is not an emergency, but exhaust leaks near the cabin can let fumes in, so do not ignore a strong smell. Replace the manifold and its studs together.

issues.t: Clogged or broken-up catalytic converter
issues.sym: The van loses power, struggles to climb hills or won't go past a low speed, sometimes with a rattle underneath, a check engine light, or a rotten-egg smell.
issues.why: Overheating from misfires or long, hard running can melt or break up the honeycomb inside the converters. The pieces block the exhaust so the engine can't breathe. Owners report this on 2013, 2016 and 2019 vans.
issues.next: Stop working the van hard. Have the exhaust back-pressure and converters checked, and fix any misfire first so new converters don't fail the same way. Converters on emissions parts may have longer warranty coverage, so ask a dealer.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The danger shows up only in a crash that sets off the driver's front airbag.
issues.why: The Takata-made driver airbag inflator can degrade and burst when it fires, throwing metal pieces at the people inside. Nissan recalled 2012-2017 NV Cargo and Passenger vans to replace it.
issues.next: Run your VIN through Nissan's or NHTSA's recall lookup today. If the recall is open, book the free inflator replacement as soon as possible.

issues.t: Gear indicator may not match shifter position (recall)
issues.sym: The gear display may show Park when the column shifter isn't fully in Park, so the van can roll after you get out.
issues.why: A lock clip on the gear selector plate of column-shift vans may have been put in wrong at the factory, and road vibration can let the indicator drift out of step with the real gear.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for this recall and have the dealer fix the clip for free.

issues.t: Shifter can leave Park without the brake pressed (recall)
issues.sym: The column shift lever can be moved out of Park without stepping on the brake pedal.
issues.why: Chemicals used when making the shift lever assembly could keep the brake-shift interlock from working on early-2013 vans with column shifters.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have a Nissan dealer repair it for free. Use the parking brake until then.

issues.t: Oil cooler bolt can break and leak oil (recall)
issues.sym: Oil on the ground or engine, a low oil warning, or smoke from oil hitting hot parts.
issues.why: Some bolts joining the engine oil cooler to the oil filter mount were too weak and could crack, letting oil escape.
issues.next: If you see oil leaking or the oil light comes on, stop the engine. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the bolts for free.

issues.t: Airbag control unit may not deploy airbags (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light, or no sign at all until a crash.
issues.why: On a small group of early 2012 vans the airbag control unit was assembled wrong, so the airbags might not go off in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the control unit for free.

issues.t: Ignition switch can turn off the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after a bump or with a heavy key ring hanging from the key. Power steering and brake assist get much harder.
issues.why: On mechanical-key vans the ignition switch can wear and slip from Run to Accessory.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Keep the key ring light until it is fixed. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces the switch for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be switched off (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera screen stays blank when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: The display settings let the camera view be turned off, and the van kept that setting the next time it went into reverse, which breaks the federal rear-visibility rule.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer updates the camera software for free.

issues.t: Check engine light for cooling fan speed (P0527)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0527, a loud engine fan, or slow shifts from first to second gear.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for the fan speed sensor code on these vans, and a separate campaign updated V8 engine computer software to cure fan noise on a small batch of 2017 NV2500 and NV3500 vans.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer to check for bulletin NTB17-105 and any open service campaign before replacing parts.

issues.t: Check engine light for low fuel rail pressure (P0087)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0087, sometimes with hesitation.
issues.why: Nissan issued bulletin NTB20-015 for low fuel rail pressure codes on these vans; the fix is to diagnose the fuel pressure system and reflash the engine computer where it applies.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask the dealer about the bulletin and the related engine computer campaign.

issues.t: No-start from a drained battery
issues.sym: The van clicks or won't crank, especially after sitting.
issues.why: Nissan bulletin NTB19-099 covers no-start conditions caused by low battery voltage on these vans, including checking for parasitic drains and updating software.
issues.next: Test and charge the battery first, then ask the dealer to check the bulletin if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, or a van that stops moving. One 2019 NV3500 owner was told it needed a replacement.
issues.why: The automatic can wear out under heavy loads and frequent stop-and-go work, and owners have reported failures on vans in daily commercial use.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won't engage, stop and get a transmission diagnosis before more damage occurs.

issues.t: Instrument cluster or computer communication failure
issues.sym: Gauges, speedometer and warning lights quit or act strangely, and scan tools show lost communication with the engine and transmission computers.
issues.why: Owners of 2016 and 2018 vans report cluster failures and lost data communication between modules, often traced to wiring or connector faults on the CAN network.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have a shop scan all modules and check the network wiring and grounds. Nissan has CAN network diagnostic bulletins (NTB13-027 and NTB10-066) that techs can follow.

issues.t: Engine stalls in gear or at idle
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while idling or sitting in gear, sometimes restarting and sometimes not.
issues.why: RepairPal lists stalling as the most-reported NV2500 problem. Causes vary: a failing sensor, a dirty throttle body, fuel delivery faults, or one of the recalls on these vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls first. Then have the stored codes read and the throttle body, sensors and fuel pressure checked.

issues.t: Transmission downshifts and lurches when stopping
issues.sym: As you brake to a stop, the transmission downshifts with a jolt that pushes the van forward.
issues.why: An owner of a 2021 NV reported this harsh downshift and linked it to a Nissan bulletin issued for the related Titan. Transmission software or adaptive shift learning is the likely area to check.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for transmission software updates and do a shift relearn. Leave extra room when stopping until it is fixed.

issues.t: Steering binds or locks up
issues.sym: The wheel suddenly gets very hard to turn or seems to lock, sometimes during a turn.
issues.why: Owners report steering gearbox failures and binding on 2017-2019 vans. One dealer found a failed steering gear.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. If the steering feels tight or notchy, have the steering gear, pump and fluid checked right away. Don't keep driving a van with steering that binds.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines can burst
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the ground, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: The steel brake lines under the van corrode, especially in salt-belt states, and can split under pressure.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have the brake lines inspected at every service if you live where roads are salted. Replace rusted lines before they fail.

issues.t: Parking brake grinding or failing
issues.sym: A grinding noise from the rear wheels and a parking brake that won't hold well.
issues.why: The parking brake uses small shoes inside the rear rotors. Rust and wear can make them drag, grind, or wear out early.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes taken apart and inspected. Replace the parking brake shoes and hardware if worn.

issues.t: Front end shakes when braking
issues.sym: The steering wheel and front end shake hard when braking from highway speed.
issues.why: Uneven front rotor wear or heavy loads can cause the pulsing, and owners report it under hard stops.
issues.next: Have the front rotors measured and replaced or resurfaced, and check the front suspension and tires.

issues.t: Coolant leaking into the cylinders
issues.sym: White exhaust smoke, coolant level dropping with no outside leak, overheating or a misfire.
issues.why: An internal coolant leak, such as a failed head gasket or cracked part, lets coolant into the cylinders. One 2012 owner had engine failure at about 36,000 miles.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and cylinder leak-down test done.

issues.t: Roof leaks and roof rust
issues.sym: Water dripping inside the cargo area, or rust bubbling on the roof.
issues.why: Owners report leaking roof seams on 2016 vans and roof corrosion on 2013 vans. Water sitting on the large roof panel speeds up rust.
issues.next: Check the roof seams and any racks or vents. Reseal leaks early and treat rust before it goes through.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags deploy when a door is closed
issues.sym: The passenger-side curtain airbags go off when someone closes a door on a parked van.
issues.why: Owners of 2013 and 2015 vans reported curtain airbags firing without a crash, likely from a fault in the side impact sensing.
issues.next: If it happens, have the airbag system scanned and repaired by a dealer and file an NHTSA complaint.

issues.t: Sliding side door sticks
issues.sym: The sliding door won't open from inside or outside, or sticks partway.
issues.why: The sliding door latch, cables or rollers can bind or wear.
issues.next: Clean and lubricate the tracks and latch. If it still sticks, have the latch and cables adjusted or replaced.

issues.t: Heated seat element burns through the seat
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the seat while the seat heater is on.
issues.why: A seat heater element can overheat and burn through the cushion.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Turn off the seat heater and stop using it. Have the seat heater and wiring inspected and replaced.

issues.t: Cargo lamp bulbs fail
issues.sym: The cargo area lights stop working.
issues.why: Nissan ran a service campaign (PC177, bulletin NTB12-112) to replace the cargo lamp bulbs on these vans. The campaign is no longer active.
issues.next: Replace the bulbs; a dealer can tell you if any campaign work was done.
